Ioannina Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ioannina, Greece

Demolished. Ioannina was home to the largest and oldest Romaniot Jewish community in Greece — a distinction preserved because Sephardi immigrants who arrived after the Spanish and Portuguese expulsions assimilated into the existing Romaniot congregation rather than supplanting it, as happened in many other Greek cities. The Romaniot synagogue, built in 1824, still stands intact today. Among the community's most notable residents was Yosef Eliyia, regarded as the greatest Jewish poet to write in Greek. On March 24, 1944, German forces rounded up roughly 1,870 of the city's Jews and deported them to Auschwitz-Birkenau via Trikala and Larissa; only 164 survived. This cemetery, presumed to date to the Romaniot community's origins in the 14th century, has been completely destroyed — the Zosimaia Lyceum and a school yard now occupy the site.
